text: Building got easy.
Finding customers didn't.
Lead lists give you ten thousand logos and zero reasons. Chatbots give you reasons you still have to check.
I'd started a rough prototype before the hackathon. Everything you'll see here, I built this week on Muse Spark.
One input. My website.
Muse Spark reads it, and works out what I sell, who buys it, and what makes a company need me right now.
It proves my competitors from their own homepages.
Then it hunts for signals, not a database. Live job posts, news, launches.
It even reads their homepage code, to see which tools they already use.
Then a second model, Muse Spark Open on Baseten, reads every quote cold, with no web access, and throws out the weak ones.
Here's a finished search for my site.
ThriveCart. Shortlisted.
Their open job post says: as one of the first three SDRs in this enterprise initiative.
It writes my opening line from those quotes only. And the checker reads it before I ever see it.
Storable looked like a fit. Until it didn't.
Proudly employs over eight hundred employees. I sell to seed to Series A startups. It's out.
The models gather the evidence. Plain code makes the call.
Every quote the checker throws out stays on the board, with its reason. Across my searches, that was a third of them.
Everything else? Needs a look, with exactly what's missing.
No website yet? Describe what you sell, and it quotes your own words.
Five companies, forty-two cents. And I can click through to every quote it used.
Now I know who to email this week, and what to say.
GTM Shortlist. Try it with your website.
